sourceRef.section: Classes (intro, STARTING EQUIPMENT, ATTACK PROFILES, Shared References)

description: Classes represent a character's primary training, capabilities, and battlefield role.
Each Player Character chooses one Base Class and one of its Subclasses.
A Base Class establishes the character's starting combat profile and grants a shared Class Ability.
A Subclass provides a Signature Ability or equivalent always-prepared feature, additional capabilities, and suggested equipment.
Class Abilities are always available unless otherwise specified.
Subclass Signature Commands and the Artificer's Field Specialty are always prepared and do not count against the character's four optional prepared Command Ability slots.

startingEquipmentConventions.finalPointValueFormula: max(100, spent Talent XP) + Equipment Points + other explicit costs
equipmentListingConventions: Standard: The recommended primary weapon for that Subclass. It is not mandatory or automatically free.
Included: Equipment that adds 0 Points to the character's value.
Optional: Additional suggested equipment that may be acquired normally.
Starting Spells: Automatically known Spell Attacks included in the Base Character Value unless a specific optional spell states an additional cost.
startingEquipmentConventions.costRule: Select a recommended or permitted weapon and pay its listed price from the Equipment Catalogue. A Class/Subclass provides access and recommendations, not a second version of the weapon or a price discount. For learned spells outside the granted starting set, use the assigned Points from the Spell Catalogue.
equipmentRules: A character may normally equip one primary melee weapon, one ranged weapon, and reasonable backup weapons.
Known Spell Attacks do not occupy physical weapon slots.
Only equipped weapons contribute their listed Equipment Points.
Armor, Shields, and magical foci are purchased separately.
The Equipment Catalogue (11_equipment_and_crafting.md) is the authoritative source for PC weapon Attack profiles and their Point costs.

This chapter repeats the relevant weapon and starting spell profiles directly beneath each Class and Subclass as reference copies, not different versions or free equipment; if a profile is later revised, the Class tables must be synchronized.
Starting Spell Attacks are also maintained in 06_spells_and_equipment.md; Characters know the spells granted by their Class/Subclass at the stated included or optional cost.
Class weapon suggestions use those exact Attack profiles and Point costs. NPC Unit Attack profiles are separate.

notes: A is the number of Attack dice the Character rolls using the listed weapon or spell before specifically granted modifications (such as Prowess or Commands).
Use each printed profile directly; apply only specific modifiers from Talents, Commands, or equipment.
Assault Phase: Ranged Weapon Attacks and ranged Spell Attacks.
Combat Phase: Melee Weapon Attacks and Spell Attacks with an Engaged Range.
Characters may acquire weapons for either phase, regardless of their Subclass's suggested equipment.
A Class without a starting Assault Attack may still participate in that phase through other eligible actions and may acquire ranged weapons later.
Charging remains a standard Assault action available to eligible Units, using universal Move + 2D6 in Structured Combat or success-based Charging in Narrative Combat.
A Charge's base Impact equals the highest Charge die, with Impact X adding to it.
attackProfileConventions.example: A Berserker choosing the standard Longsword pays its listed 10 Equipment Points and uses Engaged / A 4 / Hit 5+ / Dmg 1 as printed in the Equipment Catalogue. It does not become A 5 merely because a PC or Warrior equips it. An explicit +1 Attack die from a Talent or Command would increase it to A 5 for the specified Attack.

sharedReferences.description: The weapon/spell tables repeated in this chapter are player-facing quick references, not alternate profiles. They must be updated whenever their source catalogue changes.
notes: The Spell Catalogue additionally includes Flame Lance (Magic, Fire).

All personal CP Commands follow the active Unit timing in the full combat chapters (16_structured_combat.md); spell Attacks use the chosen Assault Attack action, not a free Attack following an Assault Move.
